fix_subject: fix: avoid cloning live SQLite inspection snapshots (#188009)
cause_quote: copySourceFile replaced the plain `copyFileDescriptorSync(source.descriptor, target)` byte copy with `copyRootFileSync({ ..., clone: "auto", ... })`, so artifact-preserving inspection snapshots started reflinking (FICLONE) the live database inode.
user_saw: On a Btrfs host with a large, fragmented live SQLite database, Gateway database writes stalled while a read-only inspection snapshot was being taken.
summary: Artifact-preserving SQLite inspection copies (sync and async) now use byte copies with clone: "never" instead of reflink/copy-offload, while offline snapshot publication keeps clone-first.
reasoning: Before #172763 the synchronous inspection copy was a plain descriptor byte copy, which does not hold the source inode in Btrfs clone metadata reservation; #172763 switched it to clone "auto", and the fix's regression test (sync inspection returned a clone/offload transfer) targets exactly that line. The async inspection path got clone "auto" earlier in #162466 (9a0146355c02), and the incident's exact caller and latency attribution are not established in the PR, so confidence is medium.

reasoning: At 7187a9afa71 the capture code (read via git show) adds all declared resources as roots and filters only entries via `!sidecars.has(entry.sourcePath)`, and that same commit introduced Memory Core's declaration of the base file plus its -wal/-shm/-journal paths, so the manifest's root-completeness check could never pass for installs with a real legacy memory SQLite file. The blame candidate d417b52 only added the rehearsal filter to the unchanged roots line. Medium because the exact header-based database recognition of the base file at that commit was inferred from its comment and the capture structure, not run.

fix_subject: fix(ios): keep streaming replies in view and stop the jump when they finish (#198326)
cause_quote: The perf change moved `self.markTimelineChanged()` out of `updateStreamingAssistantText` into `applyStreamingAssistantDisplay` behind `guard self.streamingTextShape(text) != previousShape else { return }`, so streamed words stopped bumping timelineRevision (which drove the follow-to-bottom scroll) and following relied only on the newly added `.defaultScrollAnchor(... .bottom ..., for: .sizeChanges)`.
user_saw: With the keyboard up a long reply streamed out of sight below the composer and then jumped or left a blank view when it finished; with the keyboard hidden the finished reply jumped up 42 pt.
summary: The shared iOS/macOS chat transcript now pins the bottom edge on every content-height change while following, decides the live bubble's visibility in the same pass that adds the durable row (flushing paced words on replaceMessages), and moves the working indicator below the streaming text.
reasoning: At dde29415^ every `updateStreamingAssistantText` call ran `markTimelineChanged()`, and ChatView's `onChange(of: timelineRevision)` -> `handleTimelineChange` moved the scroll position to `scrollerBottomID` while followTarget was `.latest` (always so with the keyboard up), so streaming replies were followed; dde29415 limited timeline bumps to shape changes and also split the bubble into its own observation scope (`ChatLiveAssistantText`), producing the keyboard-up follow failure and the split-pass swap the fix describes. f2c27f09 only moved the same anchor into a modifier. The 42 pt indicator jump comes from indicator-above-text ordering that predates dde29415, a secondary part of this fix.

fix_subject: fix(update): interrupted updates hang on a healthy Gateway and large-state admission times out (#193263)
cause_quote: The commit made a signal during "activating", "restarting", "verifying" call `for (const stop of admission.forward) { stop(); }` and wrapped the Gateway restart/verification in `forward(() => ...)`, while waitForGatewayHealthyRestart kept polling with `const signal = params.deadline?.signal ?? params.signal;` and ignored the stopped scope.
user_saw: An update interrupted with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM while verifying the restarted Gateway appeared to hang for up to the update deadline printing service=unknown health=ready even though the Gateway was healthy (and, separately, large-state installs fell back from candidate admission after a fixed 120 s).
summary: Makes restart readiness polling honor the enclosing command-process scope's cancellation and sizes candidate admission's timeout from measured state bytes capped by the step deadline.
reasoning: The headline hang comes from the interrupted-update recovery path added in 59834998f25 (#165863): it stops forward command scopes on a signal during verifying and runs the restart/verification inside such a scope, but the readiness poller (its signal line dates from 2b125389c8b, Sept 22, before this commit) never read the scope signal, so every systemctl spawn died and polling continued until the deadline; that feature shipped with the bug. The second defect (admission using prepared.timeoutMs, unset by default, so a fixed 120 s) dates from acffa7681f0 (#155632) and is a separate never-worked sizing issue not traced further here.

fix_subject: fix(codex): preserve native launch errors on Node 24 (#200900)
cause_quote: It bumped `"@openai/codex": "0.164.0"` to `"0.169.0"`, whose launcher uses process.execve, and taught the observer only the structured form (`/syscall: ['"]execve['"]/` plus a matching `path:` line), which Node 24 never prints because it aborts with SIGABRT and a bare `process.execve failed with error code ...` header.
user_saw: On Node 24, a bundled Codex executable that could not run produced a generic app-server startup failure instead of the actionable executable-permission/missing-binary error.
summary: The managed Codex launcher observer now recognizes Node 24's fatal `process.execve failed with error code X` header together with a SIGABRT exit and records it as the native spawn failure.
reasoning: Native launch-error attribution worked with the 0.164 launcher (spawn-style exit-1 diagnostics, #154489/#161419); the PR names #200784 as related, and that commit's diff bumps Codex to 0.169.0 (an execve-based launcher) while adding only the Node 26 structured execve branch, so on Node 24 the diagnostic was lost and the real-launcher tests failed in the hourly Codex shard right after. It could also be read as latent (upstream launcher change with #200784 as trigger), but the in-repo bump and its incomplete adaptation are one commit, so I call it a regression with medium confidence.

fix_subject: fix(claude-cli): retain deep descendant answers in any snapshot order (#193453)
cause_quote: Inside the single for-loop over message.tasks it added the gate `(parentTaskId === undefined || input.pendingBackgroundTaskIds.has(parentTaskId) || input.pendingBackgroundTaskIds.has(id))`, so a child seen before its parent in the same snapshot found no held parent and was skipped.

fix_subject: fix(sandbox): reduce filesystem stalls after commands (#200787)
cause_quote: #196662 replaced 'Changed checkpoints still pause through capture and publication' with btrfs checkpoints that 'take a filesystem snapshot, then resume', adding `prepareLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture`/`removeLocalWorkspaceCheckpointCapture` to every changed command checkpoint in runLocalWorkspaceProjection.
user_saw: On a btrfs host running sandboxed agents in large workspaces, the Gateway stalled: SQLite waits of 9 to 19.6 seconds and RPC p99 of about 52 seconds while command checkpoints created and deleted filesystem snapshots.
summary: Changed sandbox command checkpoints now pause the guest and capture directly into an immutable Git result, removing the per-checkpoint btrfs snapshot creation and retirement and the size/duration snapshot selector.
reasoning: Before 10d67445fbe, changed checkpoints paused and captured directly, which is the state this fix restores. That commit introduced a btrfs snapshot plus recursive removal for every changed checkpoint, and per the fix PR each snapshot forces a filesystem-wide btrfs transaction commit that stalled Gateway SQLite in production. d7f90ec35cf (#196727, retire captures, select snapshots only for large or slow trees) and 8ff37a6828b (#198128, skip the freeze) tuned the same path but kept snapshots for exactly the large workspaces that stalled. Medium confidence: the stall mechanism depends on btrfs kernel behavior and production timings I could not verify, and the fix is framed as an owner-accepted trade-off (about 290 ms of extra guest pause) rather than a pure bug fix.
